rv.q: The result is the best play about British working-class life since Peter Gill's The York Realist .

Cooke’s production is finely judged; Ian MacNeil’s design adds a bank of seating behind the stage so that more of us can be closer to the action, and also confronted with each other’s responses to it.
This is a diamond production of a very humane play.
It’s all beautifully controlled in Dominic Cooke ’s brilliantly cast production...

cn.t: Critics largely praise "In Basildon" as a riveting, sympathetic portrait of British working-class life, with Eldridge's sharp writing drawing strong notices. One dissenting voice finds it less edifying, but the consensus leans positive.
